title: Questions and answers on the code of practice for General-Purpose AI

evidence.quote: Transparency and Copyright, both addressing all providers of general-purpose AI models
ensuring that general-purpose AI models placed on the European market are safe and transparent
Safety and Security, relevant only to a limited number of providers of the most advanced models, subject to the AI Act's obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
Providers must notify the AI Office of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to be placed on the EU market without delay
from 2 August 2026 onwards, the Commission will enforce full compliance with all obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models with fines
the AI Office will offer to collaborate closely in particular with providers who adhere to the Code to ensure that models can continue to be placed on the EU market without delays

the AI Office will not consider them to have broken their commitments under the Code and will not reproach them for violating the AI Act. Instead, in such cases, the AI Office will consider them to act in good faith

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: This document is a Q&A on a voluntary Code of Practice that helps providers demonstrate compliance with the binding AI Act. The Code itself does not impose new obligations but serves as a compliance pathway. Full enforcement with fines begins August 2026; models pre-dating August 2025 have until August 2027. The systemic risk threshold is set at 10^25 FLOPs of training compute.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance around ensuring that general-purpose AI models placed on the EU market are safe and transparent, with special attention to systemic risk from the most powerful models. The core justification is protecting users and society from unsafe models, framed through compliance with the AI Act's safety and transparency obligations. Secondary frames include fundamental rights (copyright protections) and innovation enablement (streamlined compliance, reduced administrative burden, good-faith enforcement transition).

evidence_spans.quote: ensuring that general-purpose AI models placed on the European market are safe and transparent, including the most powerful ones
Safety and Security, relevant only to a limited number of providers of the most advanced models, subject to the AI Act's obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
streamlined compliance process, with enforcement focused on monitoring their adherence to the Code, resulting in greater predictability and reduced administrative burden
